commits.edited_message:
Fix rank-N in-memory slab indexing and support char data

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/331

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

Validate UTF-8 char data in Mat_VarRead5

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/issues/342

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect is a producer/consumer contract split across two maintenance commits in matio's MAT5 character-data handling. Commit ac50054 (edited: "Fix rank-N in-memory slab indexing and support char data") adds a consumer that trusts the array dimensions: Mat_VarReadData admits MAT_C_CHAR, and GetDataSlab gains MAT_C_CHAR cases (rank-2 and rank-N) plus a MAT_T_UTF8 arm in the slab type macros, so the in-memory stash placed by ReadNextStructField is walked for product(dims) elements. On its own this is a safe, working feature (verified: on the T_A tree the PoC does not fire, and a well-formed char field slab-reads correctly) because the reader it depends on, Mat_VarRead5's MAT_C_CHAR case, still guarantees that accepted character data has nelems*data_size <= nbytes (non-UTF-8) or a decoded character count exactly equal to product(dims) (UTF-8), so the buffer always covers the dimension-driven walk. Commit 1ed8866 (edited: "Validate UTF-8 char data in Mat_VarRead5") is the producer side: it skips the nelems*data_size <= nbytes check for MAT_T_UTF8 data and weakens ValidateUtf8CharData from 'decoded characters must equal product(dims)' to 'must not exceed', so a char field declaring dims {64,1} while storing only 8 bytes of UTF-8 is now accepted and handed out with nbytes=8; the same commit resizes Mat_PrintData's idxOffset table to product(dims) so that every nbytes-driven consumer (full read, print, duplicate, write, free) stays in bounds with such variables - which is why the T_B tree (only this commit) is clean under the PoC and under a print/duplicate/write/read-back stress run. Neither diff contains a bug by itself; the heap-buffer-overflow exists only when 1ed8866's relaxed reader feeds ac50054's dimension-driven slab walk: ReadNextStructField stashes the 8-byte heap buffer as internal->data, and Mat_VarReadData -> Mat_VarReadData5 -> GetDataSlab reads 64 single-byte elements from it (heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 at src/mat5.c:4878, AddressSanitizer abort, rc 134). A reviewer who sees only one of the diffs has no local defect to find: in ac50054 the new walk is provably covered by the (then) strict reader invariant, and in 1ed8866 no reachable consumer indexes by dimensions - the print table it touches is exactly the one it resizes. Restoring safety requires reasoning across both commits: either the reader must again refuse data whose element count falls short of the declared dimensions (or the acceptance and the walk must agree on a clamped element count bound by the buffer), or the slab walk must be bounded by the buffer size (nbytes) instead of the dimensions - i.e., the invariant produced in 1ed8866 and consumed by ac50054's new code must be re-established on one side with full knowledge of the other.
